clue.text: No chicken-hearted description of Hamlet senior's death

definitions.text: No chicken-hearted description of Hamlet senior's death

parts.words: No chicken-hearted description of Hamlet senior's death
parts.note: the Ghost in Hamlet calls his own killing by a famous phrase; 'No chicken-hearted' plays on the last word sounding like a bird, fowl, so the description is anything but cowardly poultry

explanation.surface: A critic praises a bold account of how the old King of Denmark died.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ghost of Hamlet's father uses this phrase in Shakespeare's play; FOUL sounds like FOWL, so a 'chicken-hearted' description would be a fowl one, and this is 'no chicken'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ghost's own words in Act 1 of the play for his poisoning by his brother Claudius.

clue.text: Post-impressionist shrouded in sea mist?

indicators.note: a shroud wraps and obscures, so the letters of the phrase are muddled up beneath it

explanation.surface: A painter's figure half-lost in the coastal fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrouded' asks for the letters of SEA MIST to be rearranged, giving the French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse, French painter often grouped after Impressionism with the Fauves and post-impressionists.

clue.text: Moving back in the fight

parts.note: a retreating army fights to protect its withdrawal; 'back' reads as the rear of the column

explanation.surface: A boxer retreats while still trading blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is fighting by the rear of a retreating force, so combat while withdrawing.

clue.text: Spotted, I'd say

indicators.note: this word asks us to hear the contraction rather than read it

parts.note: the contraction of I would or I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits they saw something, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eyed is to be looked at or seen, so noticed.

clue.text: How to expect a worldly inheritance from the Bible

definitions.text: How to expect a worldly inheritance from the Bible

parts.words: How to expect a worldly inheritance from the Bible
parts.note: the Sermon on the Mount says the humble shall inherit the earth, so the manner of awaiting that legacy is humbly

explanation.surface: A question about getting rich on a scriptural promise.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 5:5: 'Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth'; 'worldly inheritance' is the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes the humble, submissive manner the Beatitude rewards with the earth.

clue.text: Quick fire picture

definitions.meaning: a hurried shot taken without careful aim

explanation.surface: Quick fire picture
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty shot from a gun, and a casual photograph taken quickly with a camera.

clue.text: State in which Dad takes cover, conceivably

parts.note: dad is father
a hood is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A man becomes a parent and hides under his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the two parts; 'conceivably' nods to the state being reached by conception.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a parent of a child, male side, is a condition or status.

clue.text: Inexpert work force in the party?

definitions.text: Inexpert work force in the party?

parts.words: Inexpert work force in the party?
parts.note: a workforce without training, with 'the party' hinting at the British political party named after workers

explanation.surface: Bungling volunteers at a political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties, so untrained members of it might be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers without trade training or qualifications form this sector of the workforce.

clue.text: Contemplates ways, so to speak

indicators.note: this phrase signals that the word is said aloud, matching another spelling

parts.note: routes or methods

explanation.surface: A thinker considers different methods.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh up an idea is to consider or ponder it.

clue.text: Alias the swinging barman

parts.note: a 'barman' is read not as a publican but as a performer on a bar, and 'swinging' as literally swinging on it

explanation.surface: A nickname for a lively bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: A circus performer on a high bar suspended from ropes literally swings; the clue dresses this up as a pub barman's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus acrobat on a swinging bar is aptly a swinging bar-man.

clue.text: See 9
Second period plant

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A gardener's next stage of planting.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Overdoing it with a heavy coat

definitions.text: Overdoing it with a heavy coat

parts.words: Overdoing it with a heavy coat
parts.note: the surface suggests someone overdressed; the heavy coat is wall render laid on thickly

explanation.surface: Someone sweating in winter clothing on a warm day.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastering is both covering a wall with a thick layer and, informally, applying anything too lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading a thick layer of mortar on a wall, or laying on something to excess.

clue.text: Game at worst barely tolerated

parts.note: 'barely' means both hardly and naked, since losing players shed clothes

explanation.surface: A pastime that is just about put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game in which losing hands cost items of clothing.

clue.text: Takes from a book of the Bible

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex-works
Acts of the Apostles is a New Testament book

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a quotation from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain, as payment or obedience.

clue.text: Loops the loop, finding hazards in the way

indicators.note: to loop is to twist round, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot doing aerobatics finds danger on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loop' signals rearranging LOOPS THE into the road hazards; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes worn in a road surface endanger traffic on it.

clue.text: Enter USA in style for a drink

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new style or form, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Arrive in America in fashion and order a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white Bordeaux wine, also spelt Sauternes.

clue.text: Crazy gear Jolson donned for a song

indicators.note: the singer puts the outfit on, so his name follows the gear as its wearer

parts.note: mad means crazy
rig is equipment or outfit
Al Jolson, the American singer

explanation.surface: Al Jolson wears wild clothes to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A part song for several voices, Renaissance style.

clue.text: Fashionable pretty female doctor?

parts.note: MO is medical officer
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: An attractive woman who is a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: In vogue, stylish.

clue.text: Burdened with wealth, maybe

explanation.surface: Burdened with wealth, maybe
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a heavy weight, and colloquially very rich.

clue.text: Lodge in a ready-made position

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning a word break

explanation.surface: A guest is settled into accommodation already prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'ready-maDE POSITion', where the letters run across the hyphenated word into the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge money or silt somewhere is to put it down for keeping, as a bank receives savings.

clue.text: Cuts back to firm a form of 12

indicators.note: the word cuts is read from right to left

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Trimming firmly to shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CUTS into STUC; 12 is PLASTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine plaster used for coating walls or moulding decorations.

clue.text: Cut meaning the chop for someone

definitions.text: Cut meaning the chop for someone

parts.words: Cut meaning the chop for someone
parts.note: 'the chop' reads as dismissal but is a literal chop at the neck

explanation.surface: A redundancy announced to a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead, the most final of chops.

clue.text: Find fault with the fish

explanation.surface: Find fault with the fish
explanation.definitionFit: To complain pettily, and a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Claim I put out for shellfish

indicators.note: the letter is ejected from the word

parts.note: the letter I as written

explanation.surface: Asserting something to get seafood.

clue.text: Hard on the feet, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the word is spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: hardened skin on the sole is a callus

explanation.definitionFit: Unfeeling, insensitive.

clue.text: Accepted for high distinction on a rotatory basis?

definitions.text: Accepted for high distinction on a rotatory basis?

parts.words: Accepted for high distinction on a rotatory basis?
parts.note: 'in' the British honour the Order of Merit, with 'rotatory' hinting at a ranking order

explanation.surface: Admitted to an honour by taking turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour; 'in' it means accepted into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranked by quality, best first.
